_comment: GOLDEN OUTPUT of `chatDeepLink`, asserted from BOTH sides of the seam.
A JSON file rather than a cross-package import because the bot is a Node
process that cannot import gui-app modules, and gui-app has no business
depending on the bot. Same reasoning, and the same idiom, as
`retiredTabShape` is the CONTROL: it is what this builder emitted before
2026-08-11, and the consumer side asserts the app rejects it. Without it a
green consumer test could mean the parsers accept anything.
`teamsEntity` is the same link addressed to the INSTALLED TAB rather than
to the web. Its `context.subEntityId` is the route the tab must apply, and
the consumer side parses it with the same readers it uses on the web link:
the two must resolve to the same epic and the same chat or the button means
one thing in Teams and another in a browser.

subpath.why: The real deploy. `/next/` is a vite subpath build, so gui-app uses hash history and the route must live in the fragment.

root.why: A tab served from the origin root keeps browser history, so the route is a plain path.

teamsEntity.why: The Teams-native form, emitted whenever a real app id is configured. Opens the installed tab instead of leaving Teams for a browser, where the tab's partitioned device-auth tokens do not exist.

unsubstitutedAppId.why: CONTROL. The nil uuid is what appPackage/manifest.json carries in the repo, so an operator copying the manifest's own id gets this. It must fall back to the web link, not build a link to app 00000000-….

retiredTabShape.why: What this builder emitted until 2026-08-11, mirroring the deleted clients/teams-tab. Three path segments, no fragment: gui-app matches neither.
